1.
Ghanshyam Mishra, learned brief holder for the State submitted that on 25.12.2022 notice has been served to the informant of the case.
Despite service of notice, none appeared on behalf of the informant.

2. From the order dated 03.03.2023 passed by this Court, it appears that C.J.M., Kanpur Dehat was directed to produce the victim before the C.M.O., Kanpur Dehat for her ossification test by panel of three doctors.
As per the office report dated 07.04.2023, ossification test report of the victim has been received, which is in the closed envelope.
Today, the envelope was opened in the open Court and as per the C.M.O. concerned, the radiological age of the victim on 27.03.2023 was around 16 years.
3. Heard Sri P.K. Singh, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Ghanshyam Mishra, learned brief holder for the State-respondent.

sentences.text:
The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.
206 of 2022, under Sections 376, 452, IPC & 3/4 POCSO Act, Police Station- Shivrajpur, District- Kanpur Nagar , during pendency of the trial in the court below.
5. FIR of the present case was lodged against applicant and according to the FIR, applicant after entering in the house of the informant committed rape with his daughter aged about 17 years.
It is further mentioned in the FIR that on the shriek of his daughter, informant and his family members arrived at spot and they recognized the applicant.

6. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that applicant is innocent and totally on the basis of false allegation, he has been made accused in the present matter and actually applicant and victim both were having friendship and victim is around 18 years' old and when applicant was along with the victim then informant arrived and thereafter he lodged the FIR of the present case next day.

He further submitted that during investigation when the statements of the victim were recorded under Sections 161 Cr.P.C. and 164 Cr.P.C. then she, under the pressure of her parents, started making allegation of rape against the applicant but even from her both the statements, it appears that she was consenting party.
7.

He further submitted that even as per the prosecutrix and her parents, she was around 17 years'
old although, according to her ossification test report, which was conducted after the direction of this Court at the time of incident victim was fifteen and half years' to sixteen years' old but merely on the basis of ossification test report, it cannot be said that victim was below 17 years of age.
8. He further submitted that applicant is not having any criminal history and he is in jail since 06.11.2022 i.e. for almost ten months.

9. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that there is allegation of rape against the applicant in the statements of the prosecutrix recorded under Sections 161 Cr.P.C. and 164 Cr.P.C. but could not dispute the fact that even as per the father of the victim, she was around 17 years' old and applicant caught red-handed by the informant when he was with the victim.
10.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

11. Although, as per the allegation applicant committed rape with the minor daughter of the informant aged about 17 years and as per the ossification test report, victim was around fifteen and half years' to sixteen years' old at the time of incident but from the statements of the victim recorded during investigation, it appear that when applicant was with the victim then informant arrived and thereafter FIR of the present case was lodged, therefore, defence taken by the applicant that applicant and victim were friend and when applicant was with the victim then informant arrived and applicant was firstly caught red-handed but thereafter managed to escape, cannot be completely ruled out at this stage.
12. Law is settled, bail application should not be dismissed either for punitive or for preventive purposes.

sentences.text: 13. Applicant is not having any criminal history and he is in jail for 10 months.
14. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
15. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

16. Let the applicant- Avinash @ Chhotu be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
17. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

18. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
